input.command: export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"; gbrain setup --help 2>&1 | head -60; which claude codex
input.description: Show gbrain setup help and detect harnesses

content.content:
Exit code 1
gbrain setup <harness> — give an agent harness memory in one command

Usage: gbrain setup claude-code [flags]
       gbrain setup codex [flags]

Resolves the brain, source, transport, launcher and registration owner first and
prints them; refuses before writing anything when another owner holds the target.
With no brain configured it creates a keyless local one (gbrain init --pglite
--no-embedding). It then writes the MCP entry and hooks into the harness's own
config and verifies them with the harness_wiring smoke. Codex: [mcp_servers.<name>]
and the hook trust entries in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml, the hooks in hooks.json.

Flags:
  --dry-run            Print the target and every step; write nothing.
  --json               One JSON document on stdout (target, decisions, steps, states).
  --surface S          MCP tool surface: verbs, starter or full, listed in full (default:
                       GBRAIN_SURFACE, then the surface already registered, then starter
                       with only the memory verbs and request_tools listed:
                       serve --surface starter --advertise verbs; full is the opt-in for
                       every operation).
  --scope user|project Wiring scope: every Claude Code session (user, default) or only
                       sessions in this directory (project: ~/.claude.json projects
                       entry + .claude/settings.local.json). Codex: user only.
  --no-hooks           Register MCP only; install no hooks (GBRAIN_HOOKS=0 does the same).
  --capture            Accept automatic capture: also install the capture hooks
                       (Claude Code: Stop and SessionEnd; Codex: SessionEnd).
  --no-capture         Decline automatic capture (the default).
  --providers          Accept provider use: a new brain is created with embeddings.
  --no-providers       Decline provider use (the default: keyless, no paid calls).
  --name NAME          MCP server name (default gbrain); one name per install.
  --source ID          Pin the source the MCP server and hooks use.
  --gbrain-bin PATH    Absolute gbrain launcher (default: the gbrain on PATH).
  --serves one|several Whom the brain serves (default one: nothing changes). several labels each
                       person: config access.serves = several, a member, a folder rule
                       people/<member>/ only that member reads and one key bound to that member
                       (a 0600 file under <config>/member-keys/), then one bound read per member
                       proves it. A one-person setup on a brain that already serves several
                       people (2+ enabled members) refuses rather than write a connection bound
                       to nobody, unless this harness's entry or config mcp.stdio_member binds it.
  --members IDS        The people of --serves several, comma-separated (e.g. alice-example,bob-example).
  --labelled-only      With --serves several: each member's key reads only pages labelled for
                       that member (readable_by or a rule), never the owner's. Opt-in.
  --members-file PATH  The same, one id per line.
  --stdio-member ID    claude-code or codex: write serve --stdio-member ID into this harness's
                       MCP entry, so only its sessions read as ID (an enabled member, or one
                       of --members). Other harnesses on this host are unchanged. Use it for a
                       harness only ID uses; refused where OpenClaw or Hermes is installed
                       (give each person their own HTTP key there). A re-run keeps the entry's
                       member; setup never adds one on its own.
  --no-stdio-member    Remove --stdio-member from this harness's entry.
  --remove             Remove exactly what setup wrote (unchanged entries only), the
                       brain-first instruction block included. The brain and your
                       notes stay. Combine with --dry-run to preview.
  --no-instructions    Opt out of the brain-first instruction block (see below); an
                       existing block is removed and the opt-out is remembered.
                       GBRAIN_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS=0 does the same.
  --instructions       Opt back in after an earlier --no-instructions.
  --instructions-only  Manage only the brain-first block (on OpenClaw and Hermes, with
                       its per-turn hook): no brain, MCP or other hook changes.
                       Works for a hosted connection too, and for any harness below.
/opt/harness/bin/claude

1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)

   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.
2. Should agents save important facts the user states (preferences, decisions, commitments) automatically, with provenance? Saved facts are readable by agents connected to this brain; transient facts expire. Off any time with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback off`. (id: writeback)

content.text:
gbrain is set up and working. It's a free local brain with no API keys and no paid services, and Claude Code is connected to it. Setup's own test passed: it started the gbrain MCP server, listed its 8 tools and ran a memory lookup. `claude mcp get gbrain` also shows the server as **✔ Connected**.

**What setup did**
- Created the brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` (keyless, so it uses keyword search only).
- Registered the `gbrain` MCP server for all your Claude Code projects, in `/harness-state/claude/.claude.json`.
- Added the default SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks in `/harness-state/claude/settings.json`.
- Created a new `/harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md` containing gbrain's "check the brain first" instructions.
- Left automatic capture of sessions off (the default).

**Settings now in effect, and how to change them**
- **Search mode: conservative.** This is the only mode that fully works without keys. Change it with `gbrain config set search.mode balanced|tokenmax`.
- **Saving facts:** off, so agents save only what you explicitly ask them to remember. gbrain recommends `salient`, which saves lasting facts you state, but it's opt-in, so I left it off. Turn it on with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Free upkeep:** on. It runs while a gbrain session is open and never deletes or spends anything. Turn it off with `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- **Conversation archive:** on. It keeps one redacted page per conversation per day, and without keys nothing leaves this machine. Turn it off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`.
- **Brain shape:** none, so no starter pages. Add them later with `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal` (or `company` or `both`).
- **Auto-upgrade and release channel:** both off unless you turn them on, so the install stays on 0.60.734.0.

**Remaining issues**
- **New session needed:** Claude Code reads its config at startup, so open a new session for gbrain to load. `/mcp` should then list it.
- **Doctor warning:** `gbrain doctor` scores 95/100. Its one warning says Claude Code has no gbrain registration. Claude Code's own check says the server is connected, so I believe the warning is wrong. A likely cause is that Claude Code's config lives in a non-standard folder here (`/harness-state/claude`), and that doctor check may not follow it. I haven't confirmed this. If the warning persists after a new session, its suggested fix is `gbrain setup claude-code --gbrain-bin /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain`.

gbrain.io also offers a hosted version that can import this brain if you'd rather not keep a machine running. `gbrain notices mute hosted_option` hides that reminder.
